Berth congestion scenario labSIMULATED

An assumption-driven discrete-event model, separate from the historical AIS and Port throughput dashboard. Outputs are scenario estimates, not forecasts or observations.

Illustrative starting assumptions are loaded. Run the model to compare the configured case with the fixed example baseline.

Results appear here after simulation; no hypothetical value is shown before a run.

Simulation method, baseline and limits
  • Arrivals follow a Poisson process; vessels join one first-in, first-out queue.
  • Service time uses the selected exponential or Erlang-2 distribution. The entered mean is divided by the productive-capacity fraction.
  • The closure pauses active work at the last selected berth IDs and prevents new work there until reopening.
  • Each run has a 24-hour warm-up, then measures the selected horizon. Twenty deterministic seeded replications are averaged; queued work is drained after arrivals stop so every in-window arrival contributes to waiting time.
  • Utilization is active service berth-hours divided by open scheduled berth-hours. Queue length is time-weighted; completion rate counts services ending inside the measurement window.
  • Fixed illustrative baseline: 0.20 arrivals/hour, 4 berths, 10-hour exponential service, 85% productive capacity, no closure.
Assumptions are not calibrated against Port of Los Angeles berth events, staffing, tides, vessel classes or service records. Do not interpret outputs as actual utilization or forecasts.

Validation scopeCoordinate ranges and GeoJSON structure checked against the Los Angeles harbor extent. This is a data-integrity check, not an independent survey or Port certification. NOAA’s ENC Direct-to-GIS may support a future dock-feature layer, but its GIS conversion is not navigation-certified.
Accuracy note
Port-supplied berth lines do not certify terminal polygon boundaries. OSM dock/terminal shapes remain drafts. NOAA depth imagery shows available survey products; it is not a guaranteed current navigational chart. Vertical datums still need alignment before 3D or flood analysis.
